## Overview

Offline embedding refresh is a batch processing pattern for managing vector embeddings in retrieval systems. It addresses the need to regenerate embeddings when either the underlying embedding model changes or source documents are updated in bulk. Rather than updating embeddings on demand at query time, refresh jobs run on a fixed cadence and atomically replace the old embedding set with a new one, ensuring the retrieval index always serves consistent, homogeneous results.

## Operational Model

Refresh jobs execute on a scheduled, periodic basis rather than responding to individual events. They process the full or incremental document set, regenerating vectors using the current embedding model. The new vectors are staged separately and then swapped into the active retrieval index atomically, avoiding the problem of serving mixed-model results (where some embeddings come from an old model and others from a new one) during the transition period.

## Key Operational Concerns

### Model Versioning
Each batch of embeddings is versioned with the embedding model used to generate it. This allows tracking which model produced which vector set and facilitates rollback if needed.

### Drift Monitoring
Operational visibility into vector drift between old and new embeddings is critical. Drift can indicate model quality changes, shifts in document content, or unexpected model behavior. Monitoring this signal helps detect regressions early.

### Blue-Green Index Staging
The new vectors are staged behind a blue-green index deployment pattern. This approach allows a complete quality regression to be rolled back atomically, without requiring in-place modification of the active index. The blue (staging) and green (active) indexes can be swapped quickly if problems are detected, minimizing downtime and user impact.
